site.eyebrow: Useful things, made with a purpose
site.heroLead: I make programs, tools and resources to solve real problems. If something works, I put it here because it might help someone else too.
site.heroNote: Free to use. No account needed. Donations are optional.
site.resourcesIntro: A growing collection of practical programs, calculators, simulators, guides and learning resources.
site.aboutHeading: I made something useful. It might help you too.
aboutParagraphs: Most of the things here started because I needed to solve a problem.
Sometimes that meant building a program. Sometimes it was a calculator, a teaching resource, a simulator or simply a better way of explaining something.
Once something works, it seems wasteful for it to help only one person.
So I put it here. Not because every resource will suit everyone, and not because every problem has one perfect answer.

principles.title: Useful
principles.text: Everything should solve, explain or simplify something.

principles.title: Practical
principles.text: Resources should be made to use, not just made to look impressive.

principles.title: Adaptable
principles.text: Where possible, tools should adjust to the person, task or situation.

principles.title: Accessible
principles.text: Keep unnecessary barriers between people and useful resources to a minimum.

site.finalText: Start with what you need. Use what is useful. Leave the rest.

donation.title: Want to help keep Might Help going?
donation.text: Everything on Might Help is intended to remain free to use. If something here has been useful to you and you would like to help with hosting, maintenance and ongoing development, donations are welcome — but never required.
donation.note: Donations are completely optional. They do not unlock extra access or change the ownership or licence of any resource.

resources.pageIntro: Create handwriting resources around what the learner is ready to practise.
pageContent: Handwriting Workbench is designed to help teachers, parents and learners create handwriting material that can be adjusted rather than forcing every learner through the same fixed sequence.
Create printable handwriting worksheets, tracing activities and pencil-control exercises, then adjust the content and challenge to suit the learner.
The aim is simple: make it easier to practise the right skill at the right level.
